C0.note: Borderline. The paper predicts and evaluates outcomes of district-based plurality elections from surveys, which is a computational/statistical aspect of a voting procedure.

C1.quote: we validate this approach through extensive experiments over both simulated and real
C1.note: OT: proposes a probabilistic Bayesian model (synthetic Dirichlet likelihood) for district-based election surveys. EM: uses real Indian state election data.

C2.1.quote: the candidate/party with maximum votes in a district wins

C2.2.quote: Denote by 𝜃𝑠𝑘 the votes received by party 𝑘 in district 𝑠
C2.2.note: Single-party plurality votes, aggregated as vote counts or vote shares per district.

C2.3.quote: the underlying reality is the actual voting preference of all voters

C2.4.quote: the actual voting preference of all voters, i.e. 𝑍
C2.4.note: Votes and vote shares Z are identified with voters' preferences. There is no statement about the act of voting or about sincere voting.

C3.1.quote: Each voter in a district is likely to choose a party
C3.1.note: Voter choices are generated by probabilistic election models; no strategic voting is analysed.

C3.2.note: Truthfulness is stated only for survey respondents ('it is assumed that they respond truthfully'), not for vote submission.

C4.1.note: Input format is OTH, and no utility-type notions are used for voters.

C4.2.note: The term 'dichotomous preferences' is not used.

C5.1.note: Results evaluate prediction accuracy and survey consistency, not welfare or representation criteria.

VOT.quote_behav: Each voter in a district is likely to choose a party
VOT.note: Voters' party choices follow the probabilistic SPM/PCM processes.

OTH.quote_behav: choose districts uniformly at random, and also choose respondents
OTH.note: Survey agency or pollster whose sampling procedure (genuine, fake or malicious) is fixed by the model. Including it as an acting agent is borderline.

C8.1.note: NA: no type is STRAT or MIXED.

claims.quote: bringing scientific accuracy in the process of large-scale opinion polling
in identifying fraudulent or dubious surveys
evaluate the surveys - whether they were biased or not

C9.1.note: Claims concern real-world polling practice and detection of fraudulent surveys.

C9.2.quote: it is assumed that they respond truthfully
C9.2.note: Needed assumptions are both stated: truthful survey responses, and that votes reflect preferences (Z defined as voting preference). The genuine-survey benchmark, uniform sampling, is also stated.
